profile.headline: Software Engineer II at Emerson Electric
profile.summary: Current Software Engineer II for Emerson Electric working on feature development and software maintenance of Emerson's PLC software system, PME.

positions.title: Software Engineer II
positions.description:
I work on PAC Machine Edition (PME), an industrial automation IDE deployed internationally across water, power generation, and oil & gas. My main focus is a multi-year effort to add simulator and debugger capabilities to the product, letting customers develop and test control logic without physical hardware. The codebase is large and legacy-heavy, primarily C++ and C# across MFC, WPF, and .NET Framework, with some Delphi.
Own the Ladder Diagram editor portion of the simulator/debugger initiative, one of PME's three IEC 61131-3 programming editors (LD, ST, FBD); contribute to the simulated PLC communication layer
Simulator shipped in PME 10.6 (2024), emulating 11 PACSystems CPU models; debugger in progress
Implemented the low-level layer underneath: memory and register emulation for the simulated CPUs, including direct memory addressing, byte-level data mapping, and binary decoding verified against PACSystems runtime binaries; built multithreaded simulation components
Extended the simulator and debugger to support user-written C code blocks
Validate simulated behavior against physical PACSystems controllers over EtherNet/IP, Modbus, and SRTP, running hardware-in-the-loop testing and root-causing discrepancies between simulated and real targets
Refactor legacy PME modules using object-oriented design; profile and optimize debugger timing paths; root-cause system-level defects and remediate Coverity static analysis findings
Maintain Jenkins CI/CD pipelines for automated builds, unit and regression testing, and release deployment
Replaced the overnight Help documentation build with a local process, cutting the feedback loop from a day to minutes
Integrated GitHub Copilot with SmartBear Collaborator for AI-assisted code review comments, adopted across our 50-engineer division
Run standups and sprint planning for our four-engineer team in an Agile/Scrum SDLC; conduct code and design reviews; point of contact when our lead is out

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
Held SECRET clearance working in a closed area on the Digital Signal Processing (DSP) team supporting radar systems.
Built a performance data collection system in MATLAB and Perl on Linux, pipelining results into InfluxDB with Grafana dashboards; the team used it to track software performance across development and catch execution-speed regressions
Integrated features into and maintained the DSP team's core radar signal processing software, developing deep familiarity with the system's architecture and data flow
Compiled, debugged, and profiled DSP software on Linux using GCC and GDB; maintained Jenkins CI/CD build and automated test jobs verifying changes against system requirements
Partnered with Systems Engineers to troubleshoot cross-team issues and drive problems to root cause
Built the front end of an internal HR application in HTML and JavaScript for staff surveying and data collection, helping managers align worker allocation with project needs and employee goals; adopted company-wide for sectional and performance reviews (Jun 2020 – Jan 2021)

positions.title: Information Technology Assistant
positions.description:
Assisted with the maintenance and implementation of network problem solutions by directly interacting with server hardware and server hard line connections. 

Handled the execution of server hardware and software upgrades, directly replacing older and faulty components of the systems.

positions.title: Undergraduate Research Assistant
positions.description:
Processed radar signal data from systems at the Arecibo Observatory (Puerto Rico) and Jicamarca Observatory (Peru) to determine the location of small meteorites breaking up in the Earth’s ionosphere and the subsequent events to develop a better understanding of atmospheric wind.

Aggregated data and created graphical representations of radar signals for department presentations displaying samples of atmospheric altitude and speed of meteoric breakup, as well as averages across samples, to identify patterns in atmospheric wind behavior
